question:
Robotics & Automation

A robotic tool at $(2,5,-3)$ must reach the mirror image of calibration marker $C(1,3,2)$ with respect to the line $x=1+2t,\;y=3-t,\;z=2+t$.

(1) Find coordinates of the image of $C$ in the line.

(2) Find shortest path distance from tool to the image.

(3) Explain relevance to robotic calibration.
explanation:
The line passes through $C(1,3,2)$, so the image of $C$ with respect to the line is the same point $C$.

Distance from tool $(2,5,-3)$ to $C$:

$\sqrt{(2-1)^2+(5-3)^2+(-3-2)^2}=\sqrt{30}\approx5.48$.

Direct motion to this point minimizes calibration time and movement error.

options.A:
(1) Image of $C$ is $(3,2,3)$
(2) Shortest path distance is $\sqrt{14}$
(3) It gives a shifted calibration target
options.B:
(1) Image of $C$ is $(1,3,-2)$
(2) Shortest path distance is $\sqrt{10}$
(3) It reverses the marker across the $xy$-plane
options.C:
(1) Image of $C$ is $(2,2,3)$
(2) Shortest path distance is $5$
(3) It gives a perpendicular alignment point
options.D:
(1) Image of $C$ is $(1,3,2)$ because $C$ lies on the given line
(2) Shortest path distance from $(2,5,-3)$ to the image is $\sqrt{30}\approx5.48$
(3) Direct motion to this point minimizes calibration time and movement error
